angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 577,431 km at 60.56 pc = 0.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 16.5112 +/- 0.0143 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 60.56 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.83 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Zhang et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-880.02 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..175Z/abstract): 577,431 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.87 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Zhang et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-880.02 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..175Z/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5050 +/- 100 K from Zhang et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-880.02 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..175Z/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Zhang et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-880.02 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..175Z/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-880.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.539, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
